institutionName: Houston Methodist Hospital – Texas Medical Center

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Getting to know another healthcare system and still be able to communicate with the patients.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was so difficult getting all the information and documents and little to no help from the host hospital. You were pretty much on your own trying to figure out everything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was met a the office and placed in a room for 3 hours to wait for someone to show me where to get scrubs. I never got a tour of place or any information on when to meet or how to contact the other doctors at the department.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. I found my housing through AirBnB since it was the only place I knew where I could rent a furnished room for a longer period of time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transportation inst the best and from most places outside the medical center it is impossible to ride a bike since there isnt really any bike lanes or good side walks.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Once you got all the documents you have to follow instructions given in a mail and from that point it is fairly easy to complete the registration process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once you get the WB visa at entry in the US you get a mail with information on how to register and how to finish online courses which took me about 8 hours to completer. Apart from that youll have to complete a zoom-course about Epic. Once all of that is done, you show up at the bagde office to get your bagde and access to the hospital.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a contact from the education department to help me with the registration and to contacts from the vascular department which helped me with the initial meeting.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There arent any classes. Its only clinical rotations. A bit of a shame that there arent any lectures or so offered for the students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and persistent.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Wasnt really well planned. You were much on your own and had to fight for your change to do anything. Many of the physicians didnt know what you were supposed to do or didnt even know that you were allowed to do things.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Didnt take any since they didnt offered them.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I only went to one "teaching" sessions with the residents. Its was really good. You got to answer some of the questions even though you were a med student.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Vascular surgery 
Cardiac anesthesia 
Cardia/ transplant surgery

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The above.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Went to a conference and payed 15 USD. Supposedly the department would pay it but I wanst informed of that so I payed it myself.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and housing was way more expensive than I thought. Public transportation is cheap (1,25 USD for 3 hours unlimited rides) but takes way longer than UBER or car.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There weren’t any. You'll have to find activities and clubs on your own. I was told by my AirBnB host that the hospital had a gym you could use. I dont know if I had access to it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go see the different cultures Houston has to offer and try all kind of different cuisines.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See as much of Houston as possible. There are so many things to do outside the hospital. Go visit the NASA space center, the museum of natural sciences, museum of fine arts and so much more. Looks for festivals in your area, the original greek festival was nice. Go see some parades, the thanksgiving parade is huge and fun. Find other local activities by searching google and asking hospital staff.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are a lot of medical students from all around the world (Mexico, Hungary and so). Ask about medical school in their country and meet a lot of other students in the same situation as yourself. Often they are as frustrated as you are. Share your thoughts and frustration and figure out how they deal with them. Use and help each other.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Americans are extremely polite. Always remember using sir and ma'am. Remember to greet people with "how are you" and be thankful.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Its going to be challenging both before and during your stay
Its going to be hard to get to do anything at the hospital, but you'll see a lot of interesting operations and complex patients. 
Enjoy your freetime and go see all of Houston.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be persistent otherwise you will be forgotten.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being in another country all by yourself for 3 months.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting to do things at the hospital and being alone and by yourself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
